name: @thenextrace/tnr

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Get the current user's account info: id, email, profile (firstName, lastName, country, sport, athlete type), paid status, and account creation date. Also returns data_freshness — the most recent activity's date and source — so you can judge how current the training picture is before reasoning over it. Useful as a connectivity / auth check before doing anything else, and to ground later responses in who the user actually is.

tools.name: list_athletes
tools.description: List the athletes the user coaches: id, name, email, connected_at, tags, plans (the plans the user assigned them), visibility (how far ahead they see the training the user plans for them; change it with set_training_visibility) and sharing — which of activities, training, daily_health, physiology and incidents each athlete shares with the user. Pass an athlete's id as athleteId to list_activities, get_fitness_summary, get_recovery, get_profile, list_plans, list_incidents or create_training_plan to work with their data; a read they don't share answers 403. Empty when the user coaches nobody.

tools.name: list_races
tools.description: List the user's races. Returns each race's id, title, race_date (ISO 8601), race_type (one of: run, tri, swim, bike, custom), location, training_plan_id, and completed flag. ALWAYS call this before create_race or delete_plan — agents must reference races by id, not name. Set upcomingOnly=true to filter to races on or after today.

upcomingOnly.description: If true, only return races with a future race_date.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: List training plans the user has access to — both plans they OWN and plans they're assigned to as an ATHLETE (e.g. when a coach shared a plan with them). Each row includes id, title, workouts (count), is_public, created_at, plus a derived role ('owner' or 'athlete') and access_level ('view' | 'comment' | 'edit' | null when owner). Athletes can be granted edit access on a shared plan — check role before mutating. Owned plans also carry athlete_ids: the athletes the user assigned them to. With athleteId, lists only the user's plans assigned to that athlete — a coach's plans for them. Call before create_race (race needs a plan_id), delete_plan, or any plan-targeted operation.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes. Omit for your own data.

tools.name: list_library_workouts
tools.description: List the user's library workouts — reusable workout templates the user has saved (e.g. '6x3min VO2', 'Sweet spot 2x20'). Returns each workout's id, title, description, workout_category, workout_types, distance, duration, pace, is_course (true when the workout is a course with a route attached — fetch the route itself with get_library_workout) and folder_id (the library folder it is filed in, null when unfiled). Filter by sport when designing a session for a specific discipline, or by folderId (from list_library_folders) to see one folder.

folderId.description: Only the workouts in this folder, by id from list_library_folders.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Get the user's profile and physiology. Returns three objects: profile (firstName, lastName, country, sport, athlete type, etc.), physiology (ftpWatts = cycling threshold power in watts, runThresholdPace = run threshold pace per km, swimThresholdPace = CSS per 100m, maxHr, restingHr, thresholdHr, weight in kg, height in cm, vo2Max), and system_preferences (units, week start, etc.). Always read physiology before designing workouts — intensity targets must reference the user's actual zones. With athleteId, returns only the physiology of an athlete the user coaches, when they share physiology with them — read it before designing that athlete's workouts.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes. Omit for your own data.

tools.name: get_weather_forecast
tools.description: Get the daily weather forecast for the user's home city (set in Settings → Profile) and for each other place they keep in Settings → Weather — race venues and training camps. Returns up to 16 days ahead. `location` + `data` are the home city (label, lat/lon, timezone; data is an empty array if no city is set). `locations` lists the other places, each with id, label, latitude, longitude, timezone, starts_on and ends_on (YYYY-MM-DD; both null means forecast every day, otherwise only those days have rows), race_id (the race it was added for, if any) and its own `data`. Each data row has a date and a summary object with: temp_min, temp_max (°C), precip_mm, precip_prob_max (%), wind_speed_max and wind_gust_max (km/h), wind_direction (deg), weather_code (WMO), sunrise, sunset, uv_index_max, a 24-entry hourly array of {time, temp, precip_prob, weather_code}, and an 8-entry 3-hourly slots array of {time, temp, precip (mm over the 3 h), precip_prob, wind, gust, wind_dir, weather_code}; older rows may lack wind_gust_max and slots. On a day where a dated place applies, that place is where the athlete will be — prefer its forecast over home's. Use this to recommend outdoor session timing, warn about rain/wind/UV on planned workouts, or contextualize race-day prep. Optional: pass from/to (YYYY-MM-DD) to scope the range; from defaults to 30 days ago.

tools.name: create_training_plan
tools.description: Create a new training plan. This creates an *empty* plan container — workouts are added separately (manual or via the web app). Returns the created plan with its id, which you'll need for create_race. With athleteId, the plan is assigned to an athlete the user coaches: it is theirs to train from, and the user schedules its workouts with schedule_workout.

athleteId.description: Assign the new plan to an athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes.

tools.name: copy_plan_weeks
tools.description: Copy one or more weeks of one of the user's plans — typically a template plan only they see — into the calendars of athletes they coach, the way a coach tailors each athlete's program week by week. from (YYYY-MM-DD) is the first day of the weeks to copy and weeks how many 7-day weeks to take (default 1, max 12); every workout in that range is copied so that from lands on startDate, keeping each session's day offset and time of day. Each athlete gets the copies in their own plan from the user: the newest plan the user assigned to that athlete alone, or a new one named after the athlete, created and assigned, when there is none. Copies start fresh (not completed, no linked activity) and reach the athlete's watch. Use list_plans and list_plan_workouts to find the plan and its weeks, and list_athletes for athleteIds. Returns copies — per athlete: athlete_id, plan_id, plan_title, created_plan and workout_ids — and not_on_roster, the ids that aren't the user's athletes and got nothing. Calling it twice copies the weeks twice.

planId.description: The plan to copy from, by id from list_plans. Must be the user's own.

from.description: First day of the weeks to copy, YYYY-MM-DD.

weeks.description: How many 7-day weeks to copy from `from`. Default 1.

startDate.description: The day `from` lands on in each athlete's calendar, YYYY-MM-DD.

athleteIds.description: Athletes you coach, by id from list_athletes.

tools.name: set_training_visibility
tools.description: Set how far ahead an athlete the user coaches sees the training the user plans for them, so a coach can keep the coming weeks to themselves. mode is one of: everything (no limit), days_ahead (today and the next `days` days, 0–365) or until_date (nothing after `date`, YYYY-MM-DD on the athlete's own calendar). It covers every plan the user assigned that athlete: workouts past the window stay in the user's plans, and the athlete doesn't see them on the web, in the app, on their watch or in the plan's calendar feed until the window reaches them. Workouts the athlete added themselves stay visible to them. Use list_athletes for athleteId and each athlete's current visibility. Returns athlete_id and visibility; 404 when the athlete isn't on the user's roster.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes.

mode.description: How far ahead they see: see the tool description.

days.description: With mode days_ahead: how many days after today they see.

date.description: With mode until_date: the last day they see, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: create_race
tools.description: Create a new race in the user's account. The race can belong to a training plan (pass planId) or stand alone (omit planId). For plan-attached races, call list_plans first (or create_training_plan if the user has none). Pass segments to define the legs the race is made of; omit it and the race is created with none. raceType must be one of: run, tri, swim, bike, custom. Friendly aliases (marathon, ironman, 70.3, 5k, half_marathon, ultra, sprint, olympic, gravel, mtb, pool, open_water, duathlon, aquathlon, virtual) are accepted and normalized.

date.description: Race date as YYYY-MM-DD (or full ISO 8601).

planId.description: Training plan id (use list_plans first). Omit to create a standalone race not attached to any plan.

segments.description: The legs the race is made of, in the same shape a planned workout's segments use. A triathlon is swim, T1, bike, T2, run — transitions are segment_type 'transition' and measure in time. Writing this also refreshes the superseded race_disciplines copy.

raceType.description: Race type — one of: run, tri, swim, bike, custom. Aliases like 'marathon', 'ironman', '70.3' are accepted and normalized.

tools.name: delete_plan
tools.description: Permanently delete a training plan. CASCADES: deletes all races inside the plan as well. Cannot be undone — confirm with the user before calling. Returns { deleted: true, id }.

tools.name: list_library_folders
tools.description: List the folders the user files their library workouts in (one level deep): id, name, created_at and workout_count. Pass a folder's id as folderId to list_library_workouts to see what is in it, or to create_library_workout / update_library_workout to file a workout there.

tools.name: create_library_folder
tools.description: Create a folder in the user's workout library, to file reusable workouts by phase, session type or group. Names are unique per user, ignoring case (409 if the name is taken). Returns the folder with its id; pass it as folderId to create_library_workout or update_library_workout.

tools.name: create_library_workout
tools.description: Save a reusable workout to the user's library. Use this for structured sessions the user repeats. The description should include the structure and intensity targets in plain text — reference the user's zones / FTP / threshold pace from get_profile when relevant so targets are concrete (e.g. '6x3min @ 5:10/km'). For a proper structured session, also pass `segments` (steps + repeats) so it renders in the app's interval/segment view — put the concrete pace/power target in each segment's description. Or pass `text` instead of `segments`: the session typed out one step per line, read with the workout's sport the way the app's "Type a workout" box reads it; the response then carries `warnings` for lines it skipped or read loosely, and text with no readable step is rejected. Strength, gym and HYROX-style sessions are sport strength: exercise steps with reps, load and rest, in blocks for sets, supersets, circuits, for time, EMOM, AMRAP and on/off intervals, with run legs for a hybrid session. Pass folderId (from list_library_folders) to file it in a folder.

segments.description: Optional structured breakdown of the session — an ordered list of blocks that renders in the app's interval/segment view. Each block is a STEP (one effort) or a REPEAT (a set run N times). Give a block EITHER a `duration` (time) OR a `distance` (+ distance_unit), and put the coaching cue in `description`. Give it an intensity target with `target_type` + the matching value field, choosing the target the athlete's discipline uses: RUN → `pace` (MM:SS/km), `heart_rate_zone`, `heart_rate_custom` (bpm), `cadence` (spm), `rpe` (1-10); BIKE → `power_curve` (% FTP), `power_zone`, `power_custom` (W), `speed` (km/h), `cadence` (rpm), `heart_rate_zone`, `rpe`; SWIM → `target_pace` (MM:SS/100m), `effort` (1-7), `rpe`. Prefer a concrete target grounded in the athlete's zones over `effort`, which is a coarse fallback. Single-value targets (zones, effort, rpe, power_curve) use `target_value` — heart_rate_zone is 1-5, power_zone is a Coggan zone 1-7 (1 active recovery · 2 endurance · 3 tempo · 4 threshold · 5 VO2 max · 6 anaerobic · 7 neuromuscular); ranges (custom HR/power, speed, cadence) use `target_value_low`/`target_value_high`; pace uses `pace` (+ `pace_to` for a band). `power_pct`/`power_watts` (+ `_to`) are shortcuts for bike power targets. segment_type, segment_order and target_type (when unambiguous) are filled server-side. STRENGTH / HYROX (sport strength): an exercise STEP sets `exercise` to the exercise's name ("back squat", "wall balls", "sled push" — plain words resolve to the exercise catalog, unknown names are kept as the user's own) and how much: `reps`, `calories`, a `distance` (metres by default on an exercise) or a `duration`; plus `weight_kg` or `weight_lb` and `reps_in_reserve`. `sets` (+ `rest`, seconds) on a top-level exercise step makes it a sets block. A block is a REPEAT with `block_clock`: sets / superset / circuit run `repeat_count` rounds of its steps; for_time runs `repeat_count` rounds against an optional `time_cap`; emom is `repeat_count` intervals of `interval` (default 00:01:00) with the steps taking turns; amrap lasts `time_cap`; on_off is `repeat_count` intervals of `interval` work and `interval_rest` rest. A step with intensity run (or bike / swim / walk) and a distance or duration in a strength session is a cardio leg, which makes it a hybrid session. Times are HH:MM:SS. One level of nesting, at most 80 top-level blocks. Example HYROX block: {block_clock:"for_time", repeat_count:4, time_cap:"00:40:00", steps:[{intensity:"run", distance:"1", pace:"5:15"}, {exercise:"sled push", distance:50, weight_kg:102}, {exercise:"wall balls", reps:25, weight_kg:6}]}.

text.description:
The session as plain text, one step per line — instead of `segments`, not with it. It is read with the workout's sport, the way the app's "Type a workout" box reads it. The response carries `warnings` (line, code, skipped, message, suggestion) for lines that were skipped or read loosely; text with no readable step is rejected. ENDURANCE: "15min warmup", "3x 10min @ threshold / 3min easy", "5x400m @ 5k pace r90s", "10min cooldown"; targets like Z2, 4:30/km, 250w, 95%, 140-150bpm, rpe 7. STRENGTH (sport strength): an exercise line is the name plus sets x reps, load, rest and reps in reserve in any order — "back squat 4x6 @ 70kg, rest 2 min, rir 2", "25 wall balls 6kg", "row 15 cal", "50m sled push 102kg", "farmers carry 200m 2x24kg", "pull-ups 5x5 bw", per set "deadlift 5/5/3/3 @ 100/110/120/125"; A1 / A2 lines are a superset. A header ending in a colon starts a block that takes the lines below it until a blank line: "3 rounds:", "4 rounds for time, cap 40:", "emom 8:" ("e2mom 10:" for every 2 minutes), "amrap 12:", "8x 40s on / 20s off:", "tabata:". A run line in a strength session ("1 km run @ 5:15") is a run leg, making it a hybrid session. HYROX example:
4 rounds for time, cap 40:
1 km run @ 5:15
1000m ski erg
50m sled push 102kg
25 wall balls 6kg

emom 8:
row 15 cal
10 burpee broad jumps

folderId.description: File it in this folder, by id from list_library_folders.

tools.name: get_race
tools.description: Get a single race by id. Returns full race detail including registration_url, registration_deadline, bib_number, total_goal_time, total_actual_time, description, and segments — the legs the race is made of, in the same shape a workout's segments use. `race_disciplines` is the superseded copy of the same list and should be ignored. Useful after list_races has narrowed things down to one race the user wants to inspect or edit.

tools.name: update_race
tools.description: Update fields on an existing race. Pass only the fields you want to change. raceType must be one of: run, tri, swim, bike, custom (aliases like marathon, ironman, 70.3 are accepted and normalized). To unset an optional field, pass null. Use completed=true to mark a race as done. Pass segments to replace the race's legs wholesale — it is not a merge, so send the full list. Call list_races (or get_race) first to ensure you have the right id.

planId.description: Move to a different plan, or null to detach.

segments.description: The legs the race is made of, in the same shape a planned workout's segments use. A triathlon is swim, T1, bike, T2, run — transitions are segment_type 'transition' and measure in time. Writing this also refreshes the superseded race_disciplines copy.

tools.name: delete_race
tools.description: Permanently delete a single race. Does NOT delete the training plan it belongs to. Cannot be undone — confirm with the user before calling. To delete an entire plan including its races, use delete_plan instead.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Get a single training plan by id. Resolves both owned plans and plans the user is assigned to as an athlete. Returns full plan detail (title, workouts count, is_public, public_access_level, allow_duplication, share_token, created_at) plus a derived role ('owner' | 'athlete') and access_level (for athletes: 'view' | 'comment' | 'edit'). Use after list_plans to inspect one plan. Mutations (update_plan, delete_plan) are still owner-only.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Update fields on a training plan. Pass only the fields you want to change. is_public toggles public sharing via share_token; public_access_level controls what public viewers can do.

tools.name: set_plan_garmin_sync
tools.description: Turn Garmin sync on or off for one of the user's training plans, and choose how far ahead it sends. enabled=false takes every workout of the plan that TNR sent to Garmin back off the Garmin calendar and workout library within a minute or two, and keeps the plan and its workouts in TNR — this is the way to clear TNR's workouts from Garmin in bulk. enabled=true sends the plan's upcoming workouts to Garmin (to the athlete it is assigned to, when the user coaches), when that person has Garmin connected. With enabled=true, daysAhead limits Garmin to today plus that many days (new days are sent overnight); null sends the whole plan; leaving it out keeps the plan's current window. A coach's visibility window for the athlete still applies on top. Only workouts TNR still tracks can be removed: copies left on Garmin by an earlier disconnect, or created by another app, can only be deleted by the user in Garmin Connect. Needs owner or edit access to the plan. Returns plan_id, garmin_sync_enabled, and garmin_days_ahead plus upcoming_workouts (when on) or removing_from_garmin (when off); 404 when the user can't edit the plan.

enabled.description: false takes the plan's workouts off Garmin; true sends its upcoming workouts.

daysAhead.description: With enabled=true: send today plus this many days (7, 14, 28…); null sends the whole plan. Omit to keep the plan's current window.

tools.name: get_library_workout
tools.description: Get a single library workout by id. Returns full detail including description, distance, duration, pace, segments (the structured interval/segment breakdown, if any), the is_locked flag, and the course fields: is_course marks the workout as a route to follow, with course_route its coordinates and course_profile its elevation profile. Use after list_library_workouts to inspect one workout.

tools.name: update_library_workout
tools.description: Update fields on a library workout. Pass only fields you want to change. Locked workouts (is_locked=true) cannot be edited. Reference the user's zones from get_profile when rewriting the description so intensity targets stay concrete. Pass `segments` to (re)build the structured interval breakdown; it replaces the steps wholesale. Or pass `text` instead of `segments`: the session typed out one step per line, read with the workout's sport the way the app's "Type a workout" box reads it; the response then carries `warnings` for lines it skipped or read loosely, and text with no readable step is rejected. folderId.description: File it in this folder, by id from list_library_folders; null takes it out of its folder.

tools.name: delete_library_workout
tools.description: Permanently delete a library workout. Locked workouts (is_locked=true) cannot be deleted. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_plan_workouts
tools.description: List the *planned* workouts inside a training plan — i.e. the scheduled sessions on the plan's calendar (NOT completed activities). Returns each scheduled workout's id, title, description, workout_category, start (ISO timestamp), completed flag, and linked_activity_id (the activity that fulfilled this session, if any). Optional `from` / `to` filter by date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Each row carries has_planned_route — true when the athlete drew a route for that session; fetch it with get_scheduled_workout, which returns the polyline itself.

tools.name: schedule_workout
tools.description: Add a planned workout to a training plan on a specific date. This creates a row in training_plan_workouts — what the athlete is *supposed to do*, not a completed activity. Pass `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) to bind to a calendar day, and optionally `time` (e.g. "19:00" or "7:00 PM") for a specific start time in the user's timezone. Always include a concrete description with intensity targets grounded in the user's zones (call get_profile first). For interval / structured sessions, also pass `segments` (steps + repeats) so the workout renders in the app's interval/segment view — the concrete pace/power target goes in each segment's description. On Garmin a gym session arrives as a strength workout with each exercise, its reps and kg, and a session with run legs as one cardio workout with named lap steps.

Single-value targets (zones, effort, rpe, power_curve) use `target_value` — heart_rate_zone is 1-5, power_zone is a Coggan zone 1-7 (1 active recovery · 2 endurance · 3 tempo · 4 threshold · 5 VO2 max · 6 anaerobic · 7 neuromuscular); ranges (custom HR/power, speed, cadence) use `target_value_low`/`target_value_high`; pace uses `pace` (+ `pace_to` for a band). `power_pct`/`power_watts` (+ `_to`) are shortcuts for bike power targets. segment_type, segment_order and target_type (when unambiguous) are filled server-side. STRENGTH / HYROX (sport strength): an exercise STEP sets `exercise` to the exercise's name ("back squat", "wall balls", "sled push" — plain words resolve to the exercise catalog, unknown names are kept as the user's own) and how much: `reps`, `calories`, a `distance` (metres by default on an exercise) or a `duration`; plus `weight_kg` or `weight_lb` and `reps_in_reserve`. `sets` (+ `rest`, seconds) on a top-level exercise step makes it a sets block. A block is a REPEAT with `block_clock`: sets / superset / circuit run `repeat_count` rounds of its steps; for_time runs `repeat_count` rounds against an optional `time_cap`; emom is `repeat_count` intervals of `interval` (default 00:01:00) with the steps taking turns; amrap lasts `time_cap`; on_off is `repeat_count` intervals of `interval` work and `interval_rest` rest. A step with intensity run (or bike / swim / walk) and a distance or duration in a strength session is a cardio leg, which makes it a hybrid session. Times are HH:MM:SS. One level of nesting, at most 80 top-level blocks. Example HYROX block: {block_clock:"for_time", repeat_count:4, time_cap:"00:40:00", steps:[{intensity:"run", distance:"1", pace:"5:15"}, {exercise:"sled push", distance:50, weight_kg:102}, {exercise:"wall balls", reps:25, weight_kg:6}]}.

text.description:
The session as plain text, one step per line — instead of `segments`, not with it. It is read with the workout's sport, the way the app's "Type a workout" box reads it. The response carries `warnings` (line, code, skipped, message, suggestion) for lines that were skipped or read loosely; text with no readable step is rejected. ENDURANCE: "15min warmup", "3x 10min @ threshold / 3min easy", "5x400m @ 5k pace r90s", "10min cooldown"; targets like Z2, 4:30/km, 250w, 95%, 140-150bpm, rpe 7. STRENGTH (sport strength): an exercise line is the name plus sets x reps, load, rest and reps in reserve in any order — "back squat 4x6 @ 70kg, rest 2 min, rir 2", "25 wall balls 6kg", "row 15 cal", "50m sled push 102kg", "farmers carry 200m 2x24kg", "pull-ups 5x5 bw", per set "deadlift 5/5/3/3 @ 100/110/120/125"; A1 / A2 lines are a superset. A header ending in a colon starts a block that takes the lines below it until a blank line: "3 rounds:", "4 rounds for time, cap 40:", "emom 8:" ("e2mom 10:" for every 2 minutes), "amrap 12:", "8x 40s on / 20s off:", "tabata:". A run line in a strength session ("1 km run @ 5:15") is a run leg, making it a hybrid session. HYROX example:
4 rounds for time, cap 40:
1 km run @ 5:15
1000m ski erg
50m sled push 102kg
25 wall balls 6kg

emom 8:
row 15 cal
10 burpee broad jumps

time.description: Clock time — 24-hour ("19:00") or 12-hour ("7:00 PM"), resolved in the user's timezone. Pass together with date.

tools.name: remove_scheduled_workout
tools.description: Permanently remove a planned workout from a training plan. Does NOT touch any linked activity — only deletes the planned session. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_activities
tools.description: List the user's actual completed activities — sessions logged manually, imported from Strava, Garmin, Polar, or Apple Health, captured live from BLE sensors, or uploaded as a raw file. These are *what the user did*, NOT planned workouts. Returns { activities, count, truncated }, where each activity has id, title, workout_category, start (ISO), data_source (manual/strava/garmin/polar/applehealth/ble/raw), gear, device_name, hr_zone_breakdown, metrics, segments, and perceived_exertion (the athlete's own 1–10 rating, null when they haven't rated it). Filter with from/to (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive whole days), sport (workout_category), source (manual, strava, garmin, polar, applehealth, ble, raw). Set unlinked=true to find activities not yet linked to any planned workout, or needs_rpe=true to find ones the athlete hasn't rated yet. limit caps how many are returned (default 50, max 200) and results are auto-paginated up to it; when truncated=true there are more — narrow with from/to rather than raising limit. With athleteId, lists the activities of an athlete the user coaches (from list_athletes), when that athlete shares activities with them; Fitbit activities are left out.

unlinked.description: If true, only activities NOT linked to a planned workout.

needs_rpe.description: If true, only activities the athlete has NOT rated for perceived exertion.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes. Omit for your own data.

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: Get a single activity by id, including splits, HR zone breakdown, GPS polyline, segments (the structured interval/segment breakdown, when the session carries one), and the list of planned workouts currently linked to it (linked_planned_workouts). A coach can read an athlete's activity by id when that athlete shares activities with them.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Update the user's physiology (the data that drives training zones). All fields are optional — only the keys you provide are merged into the existing physiology JSON. ftp = cycling threshold power in watts. thresholdPace = run threshold pace as 'mm:ss' per km. css = swim CSS as 'mm:ss' per 100m. maxHr / restingHr / thresholdHr in bpm. weight in kg. Updating any of these recalculates training zones.

thresholdPace.description: Run threshold pace, mm:ss per km.

tools.name: suggest_links
tools.description: For a training plan, suggest activity→workout links using a strict heuristic: same UTC date AND same workout_category AND both sides unlinked. Returns an array of { workout, candidates[] } — each candidate carries confidence='high' because the heuristic intentionally avoids false positives. If multiple activities match a workout, all are returned; let the user pick. Use this BEFORE bulk_link_activities. Filter by date range with from/to (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: bulk_link_activities
tools.description: Link multiple activities to planned workouts in a single call. Accepts an array of { workoutId, activityId, planId } pairs. Each pair is processed in parallel via update_scheduled_workout; returns per-pair { ok, error?, workoutId, activityId } so partial successes are visible. Use this after suggest_links to confirm and apply a batch of links. Requires edit access on each plan referenced.

pairs.description: Array of { planId, workoutId, activityId } links to apply.

tools.name: get_fitness_summary
tools.description: Aggregate the user's recent training into a coaching-ready summary. Returns N weekly buckets (default 4) of activity count by sport, planned workouts, completed workouts (completed=true OR linked to an activity), per-week completion_rate %, and avg_perceived_exertion — the mean of the athlete's own 1–10 ratings that week, with rated_activities saying how many sessions it averages (null when they rated none). Also returns totals over the window and delta_vs_prior — % change against the equal-length prior window. Use this when answering 'how am I doing?', 'should I push harder?', 'am I on track?'. Includes activities from the caller plus planned workouts from any plan they have access to (owned or assigned). With athleteId, summarizes an athlete the user coaches when they share activities, counting the plans the user assigned them; Fitbit activities are left out.

weeks.description: Number of weeks to summarize. Defaults to 4.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes. Omit for your own data.

tools.name: get_scheduled_workout
tools.description: Get a single planned workout inside a training plan by id. Returns full detail: title, description, workout_category, workout_types, start (ISO timestamp), completed flag, linked_activity_id (the activity that fulfilled this session, if any), segments (the structured interval/segment breakdown, if the session has one), and planned_route — a route the athlete drew for this session as a Google precision-5 encoded polyline, with planned_route_profile its elevation profile ({distance_m, spacing_m, elevations[]}). Both are null unless a route was drawn. A planned route is what they intend to run; it is not a recorded track. Reference the id from list_plan_workouts. Works for owned plans AND plans the user is assigned to as an athlete.

tools.name: update_activity
tools.description: Update editable fields on a completed activity (typically synced from Strava). Use to fix the title, sport category, or workout type after the fact. Device-measured sport data (distance, splits, HR zones, power, etc.) is NOT updatable — that comes from the device/provider. The one exception is `perceived_exertion`: it is the athlete's own report of how hard the session felt, not a measurement, so it is the field to write when they tell you. Reference the id from list_activities. To unset a field, pass null.

perceived_exertion.description: How hard the session felt to the athlete, Borg CR10 (1 very light → 10 max effort). Set it from what they tell you, never from your own read of the data.

tools.name: get_recovery
tools.description: How recovered the athlete is, and whether they should train hard today. Two parts. `today` is the recovery read — a 0-100 score from THEIR OWN HRV, resting HR, sleep and respiration against a personal rolling baseline, adjusted by their daily check-in (mood, energy, soreness, sleep quality, stress — `wellness_score`, 0-100, null on days without one), with `band`, the `drivers` behind it, and `rest_recommended` (true on the 2nd+ consecutive suppressed day — the 'two or three low days in a row means take an easy day' rule). `readiness` is today's call, fusing that with training load: `level` (primed/balanced/strained/rundown/insufficient), a plain-English `prescription`, plus acwr, form and monotony. `series` is the per-day history for trend. Use this for 'should I train today?', 'am I recovered?', 'why do I feel flat?', and ALWAYS before prescribing a hard session. Scores are null while the baseline is still building (under ~7 days) — say so rather than guessing; `confidence` and `baseline_days` tell you how much to trust it. Sources are Garmin, Polar, Oura, Apple Health, self-captured morning HRV and the daily check-ins; `sources` counts what actually backs the read. `hrv_channel` says which scale `hrv_ms` is on: 'apple' is SDNN, which runs well above the RMSSD of 'wearable' and 'capture', so never compare hrv_ms across channels. With athleteId, reads an athlete the user coaches when they share daily health: their training load counts only when they also share activities, their thresholds only when they share physiology, and Fitbit data never counts.

days.description: Days of per-day history in `series`. Defaults to 30.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes. Omit for your own data.

tools.name: list_workout_comments
tools.description: List comments on a planned workout. Returns each comment's id, author_id, body, created_at, updated_at. Comments are the coach↔athlete dialogue layer: the plan owner and any assigned athlete granted can_view_comments may read them (403 otherwise). Order is chronological (oldest first).

tools.name: add_workout_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a planned workout. The plan owner and any assigned athlete granted can_comment may comment (403 otherwise); commenting is a per-athlete permission separate from access_level plan-structure edits. Returns the created comment row.

tools.name: list_race_comments
tools.description: List the comment thread on a race, oldest first. A race carries its own thread, separate from any activity it was run as — this is where an athlete and a coach talk about a race in the weeks before it. Returns each comment's id, race_id, author_id, body and timestamps. Readable by the race owner, and by an athlete the race's plan is shared with who has comment visibility.

tools.name: add_race_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a race's own thread. The race owner may always comment; an athlete the race's plan is shared with needs the can_comment grant (403 otherwise). Notifies the same people a workout comment does. Returns the created comment row.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List injury and illness incidents — the user's own by default, or with athleteId an athlete's who shares injuries and illness with the user (403 otherwise). from/to (YYYY-MM-DD) return incidents overlapping that window, counting an ongoing one as still running; ongoing=true returns only those with no end_date. kind is one of: injury, illness. An injury's type is one of: calf, shin, knee, hamstring, quad, achilles, foot, hip, glute, back, other. An illness's type is one of: cold, flu, stomach, fever, headache, migraine, other. severity runs 1 (low) to 4 (high) and means intensity for an injury, severity for an illness. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; an incident with no end_date is ongoing. Use this before planning training for someone: an ongoing injury changes what they should do.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Get a single injury or illness incident by id: id, user_id (the athlete it belongs to), created_by (who reported it), kind, type, severity, start_date, end_date and timestamps. kind is one of: injury, illness. An injury's type is one of: calf, shin, knee, hamstring, quad, achilles, foot, hip, glute, back, other. An illness's type is one of: cold, flu, stomach, fever, headache, migraine, other. severity runs 1 (low) to 4 (high) and means intensity for an injury, severity for an illness. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; an incident with no end_date is ongoing. Readable by the athlete, and by a coach the athlete shares injuries and illness with (Settings → Data sharing).

tools.name: create_incident
tools.description: Report an injury or illness. By default it is the user's own; pass athleteId to report one for an athlete who shares injuries and illness with the user as their coach (403 otherwise). kind is one of: injury, illness. An injury's type is one of: calf, shin, knee, hamstring, quad, achilles, foot, hip, glute, back, other. An illness's type is one of: cold, flu, stomach, fever, headache, migraine, other. severity runs 1 (low) to 4 (high) and means intensity for an injury, severity for an illness. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; an incident with no end_date is ongoing. Omit endDate while it is still ongoing. Returns the created incident, including created_by (who reported it).

type.description: Must belong to the kind: see the tool description.

endDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it is ongoing.

athleteId.description: Report it for an athlete you coach. Omit for your own.

tools.name: update_incident
tools.description: Update an injury or illness incident. Pass only the fields to change: endDate marks it resolved, endDate null marks it ongoing again. kind is one of: injury, illness. An injury's type is one of: calf, shin, knee, hamstring, quad, achilles, foot, hip, glute, back, other. An illness's type is one of: cold, flu, stomach, fever, headache, migraine, other. severity runs 1 (low) to 4 (high) and means intensity for an injury, severity for an illness. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; an incident with no end_date is ongoing. Allowed for the athlete, or for the coach who reported it while the athlete still shares injuries and illness with them (403 otherwise).

type.description: Must belong to the kind: see the tool description.

endDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it is ongoing.

tools.name: delete_incident
tools.description: Permanently delete an injury or illness incident and its comment thread. Allowed for the athlete, or for the coach who reported it while the athlete still shares injuries and illness with them (403 otherwise). Cannot be undone — confirm with the user before calling. To mark one as over instead, set endDate with update_incident.

tools.name: list_incident_comments
tools.description: List the comment thread on an injury or illness incident, oldest first — where an athlete and their coach talk about how it is going. Returns each comment's id, incident_id, author_id, body and timestamps. Readable by the athlete, and by a coach the athlete shares injuries and illness with (Settings → Data sharing).

tools.name: add_incident_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an injury or illness incident's own thread. Allowed for the athlete and for a coach they share injuries and illness with (404 otherwise). Notifies the other side of the thread. Returns the created comment row.

tools.name: list_inbox
tools.description: List the user's coach inbox: one row per athlete they coach who has a conversation with them — the athlete's comments, voice notes and direct messages, and the user's replies. Each row has athlete_id, name, waiting (true when the athlete wrote last and the user hasn't replied or marked it done), last_kind (where the last item was posted: message, workout, activity, race, incident), last_preview (its text, cut to 160 characters; null for a voice note), last_voice_ms (a voice note's length), last_from_you, last_at and done_at. filter is waiting (the default: only conversations waiting on the user) or all. Newest first; limit caps it (default 50, max 200). Read one with get_conversation, answer with send_message, or clear it with mark_conversation_done. Empty when the user coaches nobody.

filter.description: Which conversations: see the tool description.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: Read everything between the user and one athlete they coach, or between the user and their own coach, oldest first: direct messages, and the comments, voice notes and files either of them left on the athlete's planned workouts, activities, races and injuries or illnesses. Pass athleteId (from list_inbox or list_athletes) when the user is the coach, or coachId when the user is the athlete; with neither, it reads the conversation with the user's coach when they have exactly one. Returns coach and athlete ({ id, name }), data and next_before. Each item in data has kind (message, workout, activity, race, incident), id, parent (what it was posted on: id, title — an incident's type — and date, plus plan_id for a workout so add_workout_comment can reply there; null for a direct message), author, from_you, body (null for a voice note or a file), voice_note (duration_ms and transcript, which is null until there is one), attachment (file_name, mime_type and byte_size for a file; null otherwise) and created_at. Items the user couldn't read through the matching comment tool are left out, and a coach never sees comments on Fitbit activities. limit caps it (default 50, max 200) per page, and a page can come back shorter; pass next_before as before to read further back, until it is null. 404 when the two aren't an active coach and athlete.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_inbox or list_athletes.

coachId.description: Your coach, when you are the athlete. Omit it when you have exactly one coach.

before.description: next_before from the previous page, to read further back.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a direct message — the inbox's own thread, not a comment on a workout (add_workout_comment) or a race (add_race_comment). As a coach, address one athlete with athleteId, several with athleteIds, or every athlete on the user's roster carrying a tag with tag (tags are in list_athletes). Each athlete gets their own copy, so replies stay one-to-one, and copies sent together share a broadcast_id. As an athlete, address the user's coach with coachId, or leave it out when they have exactly one coach. Pass at most one of athleteId, athleteIds, tag and coachId. body is plain text, 1–1000 characters, and the recipient gets a push notification. A coach's message stops the conversation waiting in list_inbox. Returns the created messages: id, coach_id, athlete_id, author_id, body, broadcast_id and created_at. 404 when a recipient isn't the user's athlete or coach, and then nothing is sent. Calling it twice sends twice, so confirm the text with the user first.

athleteId.description: One athlete you coach, by id from list_athletes.

athleteIds.description: Several athletes you coach, by id from list_athletes.

tag.description: Every athlete on your roster with this tag, from list_athletes.

coachId.description: Your coach, when you are the athlete. Omit it when you have exactly one coach.

tools.name: mark_conversation_done
tools.description: Mark a conversation in the user's coach inbox as handled without replying: it stops waiting, and list_inbox leaves it out of waiting until the athlete writes again. athleteId is an athlete the user coaches, from list_inbox. Returns athlete_id, waiting and done_at. 404 when the athlete isn't on the user's roster or there is no conversation with them yet. Replying with send_message clears waiting by itself.

athleteId.description: An athlete you coach, by id from list_inbox.

instructions:
tnr is the athlete's own thenextrace account — races, training plans, planned workouts, a library of reusable workout templates, completed activities (Strava/Garmin/Polar/Apple Health/BLE), recovery and readiness from their own HRV and sleep, physiology and zones, and weather for their home city and the places they race or train. Everything you read and write belongs to the authenticated user — unless they coach: list_athletes lists their athletes, and athleteId on the read tools reads an athlete's data within what that athlete shares with them. Plans they assign an athlete are theirs to edit with the usual plan and schedule tools. copy_plan_weeks copies weeks of one of their plans, such as a template, into athletes' calendars, and set_training_visibility sets how far ahead an athlete sees that training. list_inbox shows which athletes are waiting on a reply, get_conversation reads everything between the user and one athlete, send_message writes to one athlete, several or a tag group, and mark_conversation_done clears a conversation without replying. An athlete reads and writes to their own coach the same way, with coachId.

Ground rules:
- Reference everything by id. ALWAYS list_* before create/update/delete — never guess an id from a name.
- Read get_profile before designing any workout: intensity targets must reference the user's real zones (FTP, threshold pace, CSS, HR). Prefer concrete targets ("6x3min @ 5:10/km") over abstract ones ("@ threshold").
- Planned workouts (schedule_*/list_plan_workouts) are what the athlete is SUPPOSED to do; activities (list_activities) are what they ACTUALLY did. Link them with update_scheduled_workout's linked_activity_id, or use suggest_links + bulk_link_activities.
- Build interval / structured sessions with the \`segments\` argument (an ordered list of steps and repeats) on schedule_workout, update_scheduled_workout, create_library_workout and update_library_workout — that is what renders in the app's interval/segment view. Target each block with target_type + its value, using the target the discipline actually uses: run → pace (MM:SS/km) / heart_rate_zone / heart_rate_custom / cadence / rpe; bike → power_curve (% FTP) / power_zone / power_custom (W) / speed / cadence / rpe; swim → target_pace / effort / rpe. Ground it in the athlete's real zones and prefer a concrete target over effort (a coarse fallback). power_pct / power_watts (+ _to) are shortcuts for bike power, and _to makes a smooth ramp; segment_type, segment_order and target_type are filled server-side when unambiguous. Or pass `text` instead of segments: the session one step per line, e.g. "3x 10min @ threshold / 3min easy".
- Strength, gym and HYROX-style sessions are sport strength: exercise steps (`exercise` by name, with reps / calories / a distance, weight_kg and reps_in_reserve) inside blocks with a `block_clock` (sets, superset, circuit, for_time, emom, amrap, on_off), and run legs (intensity run + distance + pace) for a hybrid session. `text` is usually the shortest way to write one: "back squat 4x6 @ 70kg, rest 2 min", or a "4 rounds for time, cap 40:" header over lines like "1 km run @ 5:15" and "50m sled push 102kg". On Garmin a gym session arrives as a strength workout with exercise, reps and kg; one with run legs as a cardio workout with named lap steps.
